title: Tasks solvable separately became harder in a shared recurrent model
summary: Across 100 artificial cognitive tasks, individually trained linear recurrent models solved 52 tasks, while a single flat linear recurrent model solved 14. Introducing task-specific features recovered individually solvable linear cases. The comparisons characterize the tested training setup.
ai_technology: Almost-linear RNNs; fitted hierarchical task features
organization: Ernst Strüngmann Institute; Goethe University Frankfurt

evidence.tested: The authors varied nonlinear capacity and separation of task parameters across a synthetic task battery and jointly trained subsets.
evidence.unknown: Training failure does not prove mathematical impossibility or establish human or animal learning effects.
evidence.ai_role: Almost-linear recurrent nets learned individual or jointly shared task dynamics under varied nonlinear capacity.
